SUBJECTOdyssey 9 surface party. Reconstruction of helmet recorder and flight recorder data
STATUSUnreleased

1. PURPOSE

This document introduces a reconstruction of the events of August 29, 2011 on Callisto, assembled from the recovered Odyssey 9 flight recorder and from the crew's helmet telemetry.

2. NOTICE TO VIEWERS

Viewer discretion is advised. This reconstruction is not intended to offend, or to disrespect the memory of, the four crew members who did not return, nor their families, nor the sole survivor. No funeral was held for them. This recording is the only memorial they were given.

MISSION FILE: ODYSSEY 9

Launched March 26, 2011. Five crew. Destination: Callisto, second largest moon of Jupiter, to survey the surface and return.

On August 29, 2011 at 07:30 UTC the surface party reported figures standing on the ridgeline. They did not move while watched.

By 23:47 UTC all five helmet feeds had been lost. One crew member came home.

The surface party rode escape pod EP-2 down. EP-2 has no ascent stage. Odyssey 9 did not hold station.

Your objective is the only one that matters: reach Argus A-2, the unmanned ascent vehicle at the head of the valley, restart its reactor, climb aboard, and burn before its window closes.

VOICE BANK

Each crew member has five voice slots. Audio files placed in a voices folder beside this page replace the default cuts, for example voices/baker/panic1.mp3. Cut times can be adjusted here and are remembered.

Controls and effects use NASA flight recordings in the public domain: Apollo 8, Apollo 11 and Apollo 13 air-to-ground audio and Cassini radio recordings, streamed from Wikimedia Commons.
